title: Inverse image to a geometric point is the stalk
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field and $P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

1. The global-sections functor $\Gamma(P,-):\Ab(P_{\Et})\to\Ab$ on abelian sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] is an equivalence of categories; in particular it is exact. The same holds for $\Mod(P_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod_\Lambda$ for every ring $\Lambda$.
2. Let $Y$ be a scheme and $\bar y:P\to Y$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. For every abelian sheaf $G$ on $Y_{\Et}$ there is an isomorphism $\Gamma(P,\bar y^{-1}G)\cong G_{\bar y}$, natural in $G$, between the global sections of the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and the stalk of $G$ at $\bar y$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks].

source.place: Remark Tag 04JN (remark-stalk-pullback), with Lemma Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback) (3) applied to $f=\bar y$ and the trivial geometric point of $P$; Lemma Tag 04JQ (lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point) with trivial Galois group for (1)

proof.text: For an algebraically closed $\Omega$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant] gives, naturally in every sheaf of sets $G$ on $(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)_{\Et}$, an isomorphism from the constant sheaf with value $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,G)$ to $G$. Applying this to the underlying sheaf of an abelian sheaf and observing that the canonical map is defined by restriction of sections, hence respects zero and addition, gives a natural isomorphism between the constant abelian-sheaf functor and the identity. The same argument with the scalar-action maps gives the corresponding natural isomorphism for $\Lambda$-module sheaves.

Since $P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ has one point, it is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], so by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected] the canonical map $\iota_P:E\to\Gamma(P,\underline E)$ is an isomorphism for every abelian group $E$, naturally in $E$ (it is the component at $P$ of the canonical map from the constant presheaf, natural in $E$); for $E=\Lambda$ it is a ring isomorphism $\Lambda\cong\Lambda_P(P)$, and for a $\Lambda$-module $E$ it is $\Lambda$-linear. Together with the natural isomorphism $\underline{\Gamma(P,-)}\cong\mathrm{id}$ of Step 1, the constant-sheaf functor and $\Gamma(P,-)$ are therefore quasi-inverse equivalences on abelian sheaves, and likewise on $\Lambda$-module sheaves. Every equivalence of abelian categories is exact, so both global-sections functors in (1) are exact.

proof.text: Apply the identity-geometric-point clause of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant] to the sheaf $\bar y^{-1}G$ on $P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. It gives a natural isomorphism $\Gamma(P,\bar y^{-1}G)\cong(\bar y^{-1}G)_{\mathrm{id}_P}$.

proof.text: The inverse-image stalk comparison [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ], applied to $f=\bar y$, the point $\mathrm{id}_P$ of $P$, and $G$, gives a natural isomorphism $(\bar y^{-1}G)_{\mathrm{id}_P}\cong G_{\bar y}$. Composing it with Step 3 yields the asserted natural isomorphism $\Gamma(P,\bar y^{-1}G)\cong G_{\bar y}$.
